compiled_state.description:
## Observation
On 2026-11-17, `python -m rebar verify-identity --all` in enforced mode (`REBAR_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATED=1`) on a TMPDIR dry-run copy of the reclaimed tickets history (from `origin/tickets` e7a0476397f, 30-day horizon) sat at 0% CPU while a child ran `git log --diff-filter=A --full-history --no-renames --format=%H -- *<position>*` at ~98% CPU, one ledger position at a time; an earlier run had not finished after ~3.5 h. The 8dc4 dry run also records that an enforced whole-store run did not finish in 5.5 h, so the un-rewritten history is slow too.

## Root cause (measured 2026-11-18)
Three per-event costs, two of them affecting every history:

1. **Position-map misses after reclaim (reclaimed history only).** `build_position_commit_map` (`src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py`) walks only `*.json` adds. After a reclaim the checkpoint commit adds below-checkpoint events directly as `*.json.retired`, so no `*.json` add exists for them. Measured on the previous dry-run's rewritten shadow (T0 2333118, 13,196 commits): 37,917 of 44,238 SNAPSHOT ledger positions miss the map, and so do 2 identity keyring `added_at` positions. Each miss calls `resolve_position_commit`, a full-history glob walk; the keyring misses repeat for EVERY signed event's era check. Including `*.json.retired` adds resolves all of them (0 misses left), and for 37,916 of the 37,917 the resolved commit equals the ledger's stored, reclaim-rewritten `commit_sha`. On the original history (fresh clone of origin/tickets b878d77e28d, 310,079 commits) the map has 1 miss of 44,311, and that one also resolves via `.json.retired`.
2. **One `git merge-base --is-ancestor` subprocess per keyring record per event (both histories).** `verify_authorship_at_commit` decides key-era ancestry by subprocess. Profiled enforced `--all` on the original history (first 7,553 events, 16 min): 13,266 merge-base calls at ~34 ms each = 67% of per-event time.
3. **One `ssh -V` version probe per signature verify (both histories).** `sshsig` re-probes the OpenSSH version on every verify: 6,780 `ssh -V` calls (~13 ms each) beside 6,780 `ssh-keygen -Y verify` calls (~15 ms each).
Net on the original history: ~90 ms per event x 50,418 in-scope events ≈ 75 min, plus two identical ~2 min `git log` walks (`build_introducing_commit_map` and `build_position_commit_map` run the same command).

## Plan
1. `authorship_resolution.py`: one shared add-walk over `*.json` and `*.json.retired` feeding both maps. The position map strips `.json.retired` as well as `.json`; the path-keyed introducing-commit map keeps only `*.json` paths (unchanged semantics). Oldest add still wins, so on ordinary history the original `.json` add (older than its compaction-time `.retired` add) is unchanged. Add `build_event_commit_maps(repo_root)` returning both maps from that one walk; the two existing public builders stay as thin wrappers.
2. `authorship_resolution.py`: add `build_ancestry_oracle(repo_root)`, which reads `git rev-list --parents HEAD` once into an in-memory parent graph and answers `is_ancestor(a, d)` exactly like `merge-base --is-ancestor`: a per-ancestor descendant set computed once and reused. When `d` is not in the graph it falls back to the existing subprocess; when `a` is not in the graph but `d` is, the answer is False (every ancestor of `d` is in the graph). A failed `rev-list` returns `None` and callers keep today's subprocess path.
3. `authorship.py`: `verify_authorship_at_commit` takes an optional `is_ancestor` callable, mirroring the existing optional `position_resolver`; `None` keeps today's subprocess behaviour for every other caller.
4. `verify_authorship.py`: the enforced path builds both maps from one walk and the ancestry oracle once, passes the oracle into era verification, and memoizes `_resolve_position` per position (including `None`) so a repeated miss walks at most once. Extract the map/oracle setup into a helper so `cli` does not grow in complexity.
5. `sshsig.py`: memoize `ssh_keygen_version()`'s probe for the process (`functools.lru_cache`), and treat a missing `ssh-keygen` at verify time (`FileNotFoundError`) as the existing fail-closed `unavailable` verdict. Tests that monkeypatch `ssh_keygen_version` are unaffected; the banner tests clear the cache explicitly.
6. Real data: fresh read-only clone of `origin/tickets` in `$TMPDIR` with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set and no remote; run the merged dry-run harness (`python -m rebar._commands.reclaim_dry_run`) from the fixed build; time ENFORCED `verify-identity --all` on the original and the rewritten history; record run time and verdict counts here and on the epic. Never push, reset or force-update the live tickets store or `origin/tickets`.

No config key, env var or CLI flag is added (bug-fix rule).

## Portability
`git rev-list --parents` and `git log --name-only` output is parsed as text; no fds, signals, `os.fork`, or path-separator assumptions (git always emits `/`). The version cache is an in-process `lru_cache`. Subprocess calls keep argv lists and existing timeouts. Windows behaviour is unchanged apart from fewer subprocesses; the Windows sweep will be dispatched after merge because subprocess code changes.

## File impact
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py`
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py`
- `src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py`
- `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py`
- `tests/unit/test_verify_identity_reclaim_perf.py` (new)
- `tests/unit/test_attest_sshsig_version_banner.py`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Root cause measured on a dry-run copy: the number of fallback calls, and the runtime with and without them.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_verify_identity_reclaim_perf.py` covers, RED before the fix and green after: (a) `build_position_commit_map` resolves a position whose only add is a `.json.retired` file; (b) enforced `verify-identity --all` on a compacted signed store whose history is replaced by one orphan commit of its tree (a simulated reclaim) exits 0 with zero `resolve_position_commit` calls; (c) the ancestry oracle agrees with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` for every commit pair of a small branched-and-merged repo, plus an unknown-SHA case; (d) an enforced run issues no `git merge-base` subprocess from era verification; (e) many SSHSIG verifies in one process run `ssh -V` at most once.
- [x] Existing authorship/verify-identity tests (`tests/unit/test_verify_identity_a2c7_perf.py`, `tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py`, `tests/unit/test_attest_sshsig*.py`) pass unchanged except the banner tests' cache clear.
- [x] Enforced `verify-identity --all` on a reclaimed copy of the real store completes in time comparable to the same run on the unreclaimed copy, shown by timing both on one dry-run workdir.
- [x] [non-codebase] Enforced `verify-identity --all` run time and verdict counts for the original and the rewritten history are recorded on this ticket and on epic polite-antivirus-bedbug; any history on which it does not pass is reported, and a verdict that fails only on the rewritten history is filed as a child bug of the epic.

- [x] `make verify` passes and the change lands through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
